transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
NPR has learned the U.S. is making potential plans with Israel to launch new attacks on
Iran, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
NPR's Greg Mirees says there are clear signs the U.S. is making preparations.
The U.S. is sending a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made a low-key visit to Israel this week, where he met Prime
Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Some U.S. State Department officials and family members are moving out of Saudi Arabia, so
collectively this points to the growing possibility, but not the certainty, of military action.
NPR's Greg Mirees reporting.
Trump must answer questions under oath by December 11 for his $10 billion lawsuit against
the BBC, or risk having it dismissed.
Trump sued in Florida, but the October 2024 BBC documentary that sparked the case was
never broadcast or streamed in that state.
And here's David Folkenflick reports.
The British broadcasting giant apologized for splicing two bits of Trump's speech on
January 6, 2021, together.
The documentary made it seem he had made a direct call for violence to stop the formal
certification of the election, won by Joe Biden just two months earlier.
The BBC's legal team now seeks to learn precisely what Trump thought he was doing with the speech.
After all, more than 200 January 6 defendants claimed in court that Trump had urged them
to siege Congress, quote, "show strength and fight like hell."
Trump pulled out of a deposition scheduled for last Friday, citing matters of national
importance.
Trump spent the day campaigning for a Senate candidate in Georgia, and at a GOP event in
Mar-a-Lago, his Florida resort.
David Folkenflick, NPR News, Miami.
The U.S. Supreme Court says New Hampshire election officials are no longer allowed to
consider student IDs at all when verifying voters' identity for the midterm elections.
NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports.
The Supreme Court ruling means that a student voter in New Hampshire must continue to show
at the polls a state ID, U.S. passport, or another accepted proof of their identity that
isn't a student ID.
The unsigned order by the high court is part of an early stage of a legal fight over one
of the latest laws in Republican-led states that ban registered voters from checking in
at the polls with their student IDs.
There are also lawsuits over Indiana's ban, as well as a Florida ban that's set to start
next year.
Challengers argue these bans violate the U.S. Constitution by making it harder for eligible
students to vote.
Republican state officials claim these bans support election security.
But there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud involving student IDs.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
President Trump is going to campaign today in Fort Myers, Florida.
It's part of his promise to campaign for several Republican candidates across the country ahead
of the midterm elections.
Former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigned yesterday in Mississippi.
You're listening to NPR News.
In France, officials with the famed Louvre Museum in Paris will close the institution
this Saturday.
Large protests are planned around France this weekend to call for better living conditions
and more spending on students.
Louvre officials are urging other French museums to make sure to protect visitors and guard
artwork.
Astronomers think they have a new date for when Vincent van Gogh painted his famous canvas
The Starry Night.
As NPR's Jeff Brumfield reports, the date is a month later than previously believed.
Astronomers use simulations to nail down the exact date they think The Starry Night represents,
July 22, 1889.
The researchers from Kyunghee University in South Korea say the stars, the moon, and the
planet Venus line up in a way that suggests it was paced on their positions in the early
morning.
Conventional wisdom has it The Starry Night was painted in June.
That's in part based on Letter van Gogh himself wrote, in which he discussed painting a new
study of The Starry Sky around that time.
The researchers say their results are not conclusive, but they argued the date the famous
painting was created should be reconsidered in light of their analysis.
The work appears in the journal Scientific Reports.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
The Vatican says that Pope Leo will not visit the Catholic holy town of Assisi next week.
He was supposed to join an annual conference on peace.
Leo is recovering from lung cancer surgery.
The Vatican and his doctors say his recovery is progressing well, but the doctors advise
the pope that he should continue to rest.
This is NPR.
This message comes from Cure Alzheimer's Fund.
From family to community, connections and the memories they make are everything.
Cure Alzheimer's Fund empowers scientists pursuing bold Alzheimer's research.
Learn more at curealz.org.

topics.text: U.S. reportedly planning potential new military attacks on Iran with Israel, with aircraft carrier and diplomatic moves
Trump must answer questions under oath by December 11 in $10 billion BBC lawsuit or risk dismissal
Supreme Court bars New Hampshire election officials from considering student IDs when verifying voters
Trump to campaign in Fort Myers, Florida, for Republican candidates ahead of midterms
Louvre Museum in Paris to close Saturday amid nationwide French student protests
Astronomers propose Van Gogh painted The Starry Night on July 22, 1889, not June
Vatican says Pope Leo will skip Assisi peace conference while recovering from lung cancer surgery
